title: Shift a curve, predict the result

predict.q: Bottles market: equilibrium at price 10, quantity 70 thousand. A cheaper material cuts producers' costs. What happens to equilibrium price and quantity?

options.fb: Lower costs shift supply, not demand. More is offered at every price, so the price falls.
S shifts right; at the old price there is a surplus, the price falls to 8 and buyers move along D to 80 thousand.
Price falls, but buyers respond by buying more: a movement along the demand curve, so quantity rises.
Quantity stays the same only if demand is perfectly inelastic. With a normal downward-sloping demand curve, the lower price raises quantity demanded.

task: Move the **supply shift** slider to +30 and watch E1 slide down D to E2. Then try both sliders.

target.do: Move the supply shift slider to +30, then press Check.

takeaway: S shifts right; at the old price there is a surplus, the price falls, and buyers move along D to a higher quantity. New equilibrium: price 8, quantity 80.
explore: Free play: both sliders at +30 give price 10, quantity 100.
